what_it_does: A voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) is a chip that generates radio-frequency signals — the oscillating electrical waves that carry data wirelessly. This paper describes a VCO that can switch between nine different frequency bands (each octave apart, meaning each band is double the frequency of the last), covering frequencies from 9 to 37 gigahertz. The key innovation is a 'magnetic mode switching' technique that automatically transitions between frequency bands without requiring engineers to manually adjust tuning knobs. The chip also includes an automatic frequency-tracking component that stays locked to the correct frequency across the full range, eliminating drift and manual calibration. The result is an oscillator that maintains exceptionally clean signals (low phase noise, measured as >190.7 dBc/Hz figure of merit) despite spanning an octave-plus bandwidth, which is difficult because wide tuning typically degrades signal purity.
